newsitem.title: JAPAN: Idemitsu, Cosmo, M'bishi look for Iraq oil-traders.
newsitem.headline: Idemitsu, Cosmo, M'bishi look for Iraq oil-traders.

text.p: Japan traders said on Tuesday that Japanese refiners Idemitsu Kosan Co Ltd and Cosmo Oil Ltd are each looking to secure Iraqi crude oil independently, ahead of what is now seen as an imminent resumption of exports.
Mitsubishi Corp was looking to secure Iraqi barrels on behalf of Nippon Oil, Japan Energy Corp, Kashima Oil Co and Mitsubishi Oil Co Ltd, they said.

The renewed flow of Iraqi oil to international markets has been hampered by delays in United Nations' approval of Iraq's aid distribution plan under the U.N. oil-for-food deal -- an obstacle which was effectively removed on Monday.
Exports are expected to resume in the next few days, assuming a routine approval of export contracts and a pricing formula.
Seven Japanese oil companies purchased Iraq's Basrah Light for delivery in the oil deal's first 180 days.

Trading house Mitsubishi Corp -- acting on behalf of Nippon Oil, Japan Energy, Kashima Oil Co, Showa Shell Sekiyu KK and Mitsubishi Oil Co Ltd -- bought a total of 20,000 barrels per day (bpd) of Basrah Light crude.
Cosmo and Idemitsu each purchased 900,000 barrels in direct negotiations with Iraq.
